chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If there is upon a man something from the fasting of the month of Ramadan, let him make it up in whichever months he wishes, consecutive days. If he is unable, let him make it up however he wishes and let him count the days. If he separates them, it is good, and if he continues them, it is good.
I said: What do you think if there remains upon him something from the fasting of Ramadan - should he make it up in Dhu al-Hijjah? He said: Yes.

key_terms.ذِي اَلْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for making up missed days of Ramadan fasting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in compensating for missed Ramadan fasts, emphasizing that continuity (mutatabi'an) is not mandatory but rather a matter of personal ease. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of removing hardship, allowing the believer to choose between consecutive or scattered days based on their capacity. The specific confirmation regarding Dhu al-Hijjah addresses potential concerns about fasting during this sacred month, affirming its permissibility for qada.
